   Forum: MOM considers circumstances of workers when investigating work pass offences
 Sign up now: Get ST's newsletters delivered to your inbox
 Published   Nov 12, 2026, 06:00 PM
 Updated   Nov 12, 2026, 06:00 PM
 Set as preferred source Listen We refer to the Forum letter, “ Enforcement on work pass offences must also protect deceived workers ” (Nov 4).
 The Ministry of Manpower (MOM) takes a serious view of work pass offences, including false declarations and illegal deployment of migrant workers. Such practices undermine the integrity of our work pass framework and expose workers to exploitation.
 The ministry will take firm action against those found responsible.
 When investigating work pass offences, MOM adopts a holistic approach, taking into account the circumstances of each case. We assess each individual’s culpability, including their role and extent of involvement, when determining the appropriate enforcement action.
 While some workers may have been misled into accepting arrangements that contravene work pass requirements, others may have knowingly participated in or facilitated such unlawful arrangements, including helping to recruit other workers.
 Where workers require assistance, MOM works with partners such as the Migrant Workers’ Centre to address their concerns, including assistance with salary claims where applicable.
 We encourage migrant workers who are facing difficulties or have concerns about their employment conditions to approach MOM early for assistance through our hotline on 6438 5122 or the “Talk to MOM” function on the FWMOMCare mobile app.
 Adrian Quek 
Divisional Director
Foreign Manpower Management Division
